subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: An eigenvector must be
solution_latex: The zero vector satisfies Av=λv for every λ and is excluded to keep the concept meaningful.
common_mistake: Normalization is optional.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Eigenvalues of a triangular matrix are
solution_latex: The characteristic determinant of a triangular matrix is the product of diagonal shifts.
common_mistake: Off-diagonal entries can affect eigenvectors but not eigenvalues.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: For a real symmetric matrix, eigenvalues are
solution_latex: The spectral theorem guarantees real eigenvalues.
common_mistake: Symmetry does not imply positive definiteness.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix are
solution_latex: Symmetry makes eigenspaces for distinct eigenvalues orthogonal.
common_mistake: This orthogonality need not hold for nonsymmetric matrices.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A matrix is diagonalizable when it has
solution_latex: An n×n matrix needs n independent eigenvectors to form the diagonalizing basis.
common_mistake: Invertibility and diagonalizability are different.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Trace equals
solution_latex: The characteristic polynomial coefficients give trace as eigenvalue sum.
common_mistake: Determinant is the eigenvalue product.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: For A=PDP inverse, which are true?
options: A and D have the same eigenvalues
solution_latex: Similarity preserves spectrum, P collects an eigenbasis, and powers act on D.
common_mistake: D stores eigenvalues and need not be identity.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A repeated eigenvalue guarantees diagonalizability
options: only if geometric multiplicity reaches algebraic multiplicity
solution_latex: Every eigenvalue must supply enough independent eigenvectors.
common_mistake: Repetition alone does not decide diagonalizability.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: If Av=λv, then A²v equals
solution_latex: A²v=A(λv)=λAv=λ²v.
common_mistake: The power applies to the eigenvalue.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Zero is an eigenvalue exactly when A is
solution_latex: Av=0 has a nonzero solution exactly when A is singular.
common_mistake: A symmetric matrix can be invertible.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter eigenvalue sum of a matrix with trace 9.
solution_latex: Eigenvalues sum to trace, counting algebraic multiplicity.
common_mistake: No diagonalization is needed.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A 3×3 matrix has eigenvalues 1,2,4. Enter its determinant.
solution_latex: The product is 1·2·4=8.
common_mistake: Determinant uses product, not sum.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter the largest eigenvalue of diag(−2,5,3).
solution_latex: Diagonal entries are the eigenvalues.
common_mistake: Largest means algebraically largest here.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: If Av=3v, enter the eigenvalue of A⁵ for the same v.
solution_latex: A⁵v=3⁵v=243v.
common_mistake: Raise the eigenvalue to the power.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A 2×2 matrix has trace 7 and one eigenvalue 2. Enter the other.
solution_latex: The eigenvalues sum to 7, so the other is 5.
common_mistake: Trace counts multiplicity.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A 2×2 matrix has determinant 12 and one eigenvalue 3. Enter the other.
solution_latex: Eigenvalue product is 12, so the other is 4.
common_mistake: Use determinant for product.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter the geometric multiplicity of eigenvalue 1 for [[1,1],[0,1]].
solution_latex: A−I has rank 1, so its null space is one-dimensional.
common_mistake: Algebraic multiplicity is 2 but geometric multiplicity is 1.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A real symmetric 4×4 matrix has four distinct eigenvalues. Enter the maximum size of an orthonormal eigenbasis.
solution_latex: The spectral theorem supplies four orthonormal eigenvectors.
common_mistake: Distinctness already gives independent vectors; symmetry gives orthogonality.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: If eigenvalues of A are 2 and −1, enter trace(A³).
solution_latex: Eigenvalues of A³ are 8 and −1, so trace is 7.
common_mistake: Cube eigenvalues before summing.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter the spectral radius of diag(−6,2,5).
solution_latex: Spectral radius is maximum absolute eigenvalue: max(6,2,5)=6.
common_mistake: Use absolute magnitude, not largest signed value.
